author: Grace Chen
title: Dr. Floridalia Demands Justice After Aggression, Walks to MP
text:
A medical professional’s distinctive protest drew attention this Wednesday when Dr. Floridalia Aguilar walked from the Toncontín sector to the Public Ministry facilities. The doctor, who previously went viral for protesting in a swimsuit, walked under the strong midday sun. She was demanding her case file from the Women’s Prosecutor’s Office . She had requested the documents since August 18.
Dr. Aguilar explained she urgently needs the paperwork to proceed with her complaint. She filed it against Óscar David Montecinos Medina, an employee of the 911 emergency system and an activist. Montecinos verbally assaulted Dr. Aguilar on May 1 during a May Day march in the capital. The altercation was recorded and went viral, sparking widespread criticism of the public employee’s actions toward a woman peacefully protesting.
Oscar David Montecinos insults and makes obscene to Dr. Floridalia on May 1, 2025 in Tegucigalpa. “I thank the drivers who did not hit me, because you remember that living in Honduras is a risk every day,” she lamented, highlighting her unusual approach to seeking justice.
Seeking Impartial Justice Dr. Aguilar emphasized that the initial hearing in the Capital Courts is scheduled for September 11. She is demanding that justice be served impartially.
“I want my complaint to have a non-politicized, non-partialized turn,” she stated. “I want the Women’s Prosecutor not to partialized in favor of this public servant of 911. I will not allow them to partialized; my physical aggression has caused me a lot of damage. Just as that aggression was in the streets, I am going to ask for justice in the streets, Honduran town.”
Floridalia Aguilar walks along the European Economic Community Boulevard at noon on Wednesday, September 3, 2025. Dr. Aguilar’s protest proved effective. The Women’s Prosecutor’s Office provided the necessary documentation. She will now proceed before the judge. She vowed to continue until justice is served in her case and for all women who feel let down by the Public Ministry.
